title: Harry Sosnick, joining Isham Jones and the Isham Jones Juniors
summary: After about two and a half years with Garen he joined Harry Sosnick's radio band, then Isham Jones, where he made his first musical recordings and led the Juniors small group.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Yes, and I stayed with Tom for about -- oh, I guess two and a half years. And when I did leave him it was supposedly to start my own group. And I ran into so many roadblocks that I wound up joining another band because I couldn't stand the waiting around for something to happen. And so I joined Harry Sosnick's band, which was a radio band, and doing one of its earliest and first and only tours, I think. And that band, we had some very fine musicians, mostly from the Chicago area. And I think it was a good transition move for me. But I finally got -- the best place to be for someone like myself at that point was to be with a band which was really musical and only concerned with music.

And I was growing a little bored with doing my show biz, once again. So I got this offer to go with Isham Jones, and the reason I got the offer was because about four or five guys in the band were friends of mine and knew what I could do musically, and got me the job with Isham.
But even someone who was a great songwriter and a

very good arranger, and a very good all-around musician, someone like Isham Jones, who certainly had a very good musical background, hired me, I think, mainly because he heard I could sing, dance, if necessary, and do many things, and because he knew a lot of saxophone players. It was as basic as that.

And -- however, it gave me a chance to prove what I wanted to do somewhat musically, and with -- my first actual recording dates were with the Isham Jones band. I did some earlier with Tom Garen's band, but they were once again entertainment quality records. And this was my first -- little more musical experience, and eventually we had -- our first jazz date was done as a small group, and we were the Isham Jones Juniors. And it was really my group, along with the rhythm section and maybe a trumpet, and Joe Bishop on flugelhorn or something.

So it was a good experience for me, and as a matter of fact, we all by that point -- I did especially, had my own desires as to where -- what kind of music to play. And I was certainly interested in the jazz of that time. And the Ben Pollack band was a great favorite of mine, along with Benny's band and everyone else who was into playing swinging music.
